source.text: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ· ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: They called therefore the man out of second [time] who was blind, and said to him, "Give glory to the God; we know that this the man a sinner is."

en.L: So for a second [time] they called the man who had been blind, and said to him, "Give glory to God; we know that this man is a sinner."
en.B: So they summoned the man who had been blind a second time and said to him, "Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner."
en.R: So the Jewish leaders called back the man who had been blind. They said to him, "Give glory to God by telling the truth! We know that this man is a sinner."

es.L: Llamaron, pues, por segunda vez al hombre que había sido ciego, y le dijeron: «Da gloria a Dios; nosotros sabemos que este hombre es pecador».
es.B: Así que llamaron por segunda vez al hombre que había sido ciego y le dijeron: «Da gloria a Dios. Nosotros sabemos que este hombre es pecador».
es.R: Entonces los dirigentes judíos volvieron a llamar al hombre que había sido ciego. Le dijeron: «¡Da gloria a Dios diciendo la verdad! Nosotros sabemos que este hombre es pecador».

fr.L: Ils appelèrent donc une seconde fois l’homme qui avait été aveugle, et lui dirent : « Rends gloire à Dieu ; nous, nous savons que cet homme est un pécheur. »
fr.B: Ils convoquèrent donc une deuxième fois l’homme qui avait été aveugle et lui dirent : « Rends gloire à Dieu. Nous savons, nous, que cet homme est un pécheur. »
fr.R: Alors les chefs juifs ont fait revenir l’homme qui avait été aveugle. Ils lui ont dit : « Rends gloire à Dieu en disant la vérité ! Nous savons que cet homme est un pécheur. »

sw.B: Basi wakamwita mara ya pili yule mtu aliyekuwa kipofu, wakamwambia, "Mpe Mungu utukufu. Tunajua kwamba mtu huyu ni mwenye dhambi."

vi.L: Vậy họ gọi người trước kia bị mù đến lần thứ hai, và nói với anh ta: "Hãy dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời; chúng tôi biết người này là người tội lỗi."
vi.B: Vậy họ cho gọi người trước kia bị mù đến lần thứ hai và nói: "Hãy dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời. Chúng tôi biết người này là một người tội lỗi."
vi.R: Vậy các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái gọi người trước kia bị mù trở lại. Họ nói với anh ta: "Hãy nói thật để dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời! Chúng tôi biết người này là một người tội lỗi."

ko.L: 그래서 그들이 눈멀었던 그 사람을 두 번째로 불러 그에게 말했다. "하나님께 영광을 돌려라. 우리는 이 사람이 죄인이라는 것을 안다."
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 눈멀었던 그 사람을 다시 불러서 말했다. "하나님께 영광을 돌려라. 우리는 이 사람이 죄인이라는 것을 알고 있다."
ko.R: 그래서 유대 지도자들은 눈멀었던 그 사람을 다시 불러서 말했다. "사실대로 말해서 하나님께 영광을 돌려라! 우리는 이 사람이 죄인이라는 것을 알고 있다."

pt.L: Então chamaram pela segunda [vez] o homem que tinha sido cego e lhe disseram: "Dê glória a Deus; nós sabemos que este homem é pecador."
pt.B: Então chamaram pela segunda vez o homem que tinha sido cego e lhe disseram: "Dê glória a Deus. Nós sabemos que esse homem é um pecador."
pt.R: Então os líderes judeus chamaram de volta o homem que tinha sido cego. Eles lhe disseram: "Dê glória a Deus contando a verdade! Nós sabemos que esse homem é um pecador."

am.L: ስለዚህ ዕውር የነበረውን ሰው ለሁለተኛ ጊዜ ጠሩት፤ እንዲህም አሉት፦ «ለእግዚአብሔር ክብርን ስጥ፤ እኛ ይህ ሰው ኃጢአተኛ እንደሆነ እናውቃለን።»
am.B: ስለዚህ ዕውር የነበረውን ሰው ለሁለተኛ ጊዜ አስጠርተው እንዲህ አሉት፦ «ለእግዚአብሔር ክብር ስጥ። ይህ ሰው ኃጢአተኛ መሆኑን እናውቃለን።»
am.R: ስለዚህ የአይሁድ መሪዎች ዓይነ ስውር የነበረውን ሰው እንደገና ጠሩት። እንዲህም አሉት፦ «እውነቱን በመናገር ለእግዚአብሔር ክብር ስጥ! ይህ ሰው ኃጢአተኛ መሆኑን እናውቃለን።»

decisions.choice: Give glory to God: a solemn charge to tell the truth in God's presence
alternatives: give God, not Jesus, the praise for the healing
decisions.reason: The words are a set formula for putting someone under oath. Joshua says them to Achan before Achan confesses what he had taken (Joshua 7:19), and the sense there is: own the truth before God, who sees it. The leaders demand that the man stop defending the healer and admit what they think is the truth. Some read the words as "thank God for your sight, not this man", and that thought may be present as well, but the formula and the setting of a hearing point first to the oath. A footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: glory: the honor that belongs to God
decisions.reason: Key term. To give God glory is to honor him as he deserves; here that means honoring him by speaking the truth before him (meaning decision m1). The irony is that the man's honest testimony is exactly what gives God glory (compare 9:3, so that the works of God might be shown in him).

decisions.choice: we know: the pronoun is emphatic; the leaders speak with the authority of teachers of the law
decisions.reason: They set their verdict against the man's story: whatever happened, they know what Jesus is. The phrase "we know" runs through the rest of the passage. The man answers that he does not know this (9:25); they claim to know that God spoke to Moses but not where Jesus comes from (9:29); and the man turns their words back on them (9:31).

decisions.choice: a sinner: one who breaks God's law, here by working on the Sabbath
alternatives: a sinner in the general sense that all people sin
decisions.reason: Some of the Pharisees had already said that Jesus was not from God because he did not keep the Sabbath (9:14-16). He had made mud and healed on that day. For them this settled the matter: a man who breaks the law in this way is a sinner and cannot have been sent by God.

decisions.choice: a second time: the leaders call the man back after questioning his parents
decisions.reason: They had questioned him once (9:15-17), and then his parents (9:18-23). Now they call him in again.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders; by telling the truth
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers, the authorities who questioned the man and his parents (9:13-23), and says what the formula "give glory to God" asks of him (meaning decision m1). It keeps the word "glory".

decisions.choice: los dirigentes judíos; diciendo la verdad
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the speakers and says what the formula means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for this passage (9:24-34). The passé simple ("ils appelèrent", "il répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("ils ont fait revenir"), the past tense young readers know. John has no historic present in this passage. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je vous l’ai déjà dit", "Dieu a parlé à Moïse").

decisions.choice: Rends gloire à Dieu
decisions.reason: "Rendre gloire à Dieu" is the set French expression for giving God the glory due to him, which suits a formula of oath (meaning decision m1); "donner gloire" is a calque. Readable adds "en disant la vérité", as the English does, and keeps "gloire", the key term.

decisions.choice: "dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: Keeps the key term "vinh quang" in a solemn formula; Readable adds "nói thật" as the English does.

decisions.choice: the leaders call the man "anh" and themselves "chúng tôi"; they call Jesus "người này", "ông ta"; the man calls Jesus "ông ấy"
decisions.reason: The forms used through 9:13-34. Vietnamese speakers in a quarrel often drop to "mày"; it was not used here so that the scorn is carried by the words ("dám", "người đó") rather than by a coarse pronoun.

decisions.choice: The leaders speak to the man in the plain style (해라체: -라, -다); he answers in the formal style (합쇼체), calling them "여러분"
alternatives: the formal style on both sides
decisions.reason: The style guide's defaults for authorities and a man before them. The speech levels hold through the whole hearing (9:24-34) and make the leaders' scorn and the man's boldness within polite forms audible.

decisions.choice: "사실대로 말해서" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom is a solemn charge to tell the truth (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ዕውር" (blind, L, B); "ዓይነ ስውር" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew and 9:13-23: "ዕውር" is the plain written word, and Readable uses the gentler everyday "ዓይነ ስውር". Used for the whole passage.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος· Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα· ἓν οἶδα ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω.

records.literal_gloss: Answered therefore that [one], "If a sinner he is, not I know; one [thing] I know, that blind being, now I see."

en.L: So that [man] answered, "Whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a sinner, I do not know; one [thing] I know, that being blind, now I see."
en.B: He answered, "Whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a sinner, I do not know. I do know one thing: I used to be blind, and now I can see."
en.R: The man answered, "I do not know if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a sinner. But there is one thing I do know. Before, I could not see. Now I can!"

es.L: Respondió, pues, aquel: «Si es pecador, no lo sé; una cosa sé: que, siendo ciego, ahora veo».
es.B: Él respondió: «Si es pecador o no, no lo sé. Lo que sí sé es una cosa: yo era ciego, y ahora veo».
es.R: El hombre respondió: «No sé si es pecador. Pero hay una cosa que sí sé. Antes no podía ver. ¡Ahora sí!».

fr.L: Celui-là répondit donc : « S’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est un pécheur, je ne [le] sais pas ; je sais une chose : étant aveugle, maintenant je vois. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « S’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est un pécheur, je n’en sais rien. Mais il y a une chose que je sais : moi qui étais aveugle, maintenant je vois. »
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : « Je ne sais pas s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est un pécheur. Mais il y a une chose que je sais bien. Avant, je ne voyais pas. Maintenant, je vois ! »

sw.L: Basi yule akajibu, "Kama yeye ni mtenda dhambi, mimi sijui; ninajua jambo moja, kwamba nikiwa kipofu, sasa ninaona."

vi.L: Vậy người ấy đáp: "Ông ấy có phải là người tội lỗi hay không, tôi không biết; một [điều] tôi biết, là tôi vốn bị mù, nay tôi thấy."

vi.R: Người ấy trả lời: "Tôi không biết ông ấy có phải là người tội lỗi không. Nhưng có một điều tôi biết. Trước đây tôi không thấy gì. Bây giờ tôi thấy được!"

pt.L: Então aquele [homem] respondeu: "Se {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é pecador, não sei; uma [coisa] sei: que, sendo cego, agora vejo."
pt.B: Ele respondeu: "Se {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é pecador, não sei. Uma coisa eu sei: eu era cego e agora enxergo."
pt.R: O homem respondeu: "Eu não sei se {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é pecador. Mas uma coisa eu sei. Antes eu não enxergava. Agora eu enxergo!"

am.L: ስለዚህ ያ [ሰው] እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ኃጢአተኛ ይሁን አይሁን አላውቅም፤ አንድ [ነገር] አውቃለሁ፤ ዕውር የነበርኩት አሁን አያለሁ።»
am.B: እርሱም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ኃጢአተኛ ይሁን አይሁን አላውቅም። አንድ ነገር ግን አውቃለሁ፤ ዕውር ነበርኩ፤ አሁን ግን አያለሁ።»
am.R: ሰውየውም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ኃጢአተኛ መሆን አለመሆኑን አላውቅም። ነገር ግን አንድ የማውቀው ነገር አለ። ከዚህ በፊት ማየት አልችልም ነበር። አሁን ግን አያለሁ!»

decisions.choice: whether he is a sinner, I do not know: he will not give the verdict they demand
alternatives: If he is a sinner, I do not know it (a denial that he is one)
decisions.reason: The "if" introduces an indirect question, as often after "know". The man neither agrees nor openly disagrees. He leaves the question of the law to them and holds to what he can say for himself. By 9:31-33 he will draw the conclusion they refuse.

decisions.choice: being blind, now I see: the participle stands for his former state, set against "now"
alternatives: although I am blind, I see
decisions.reason: The present participle describes what he was, a man blind from birth, and "now" marks the change. The sentence sets two plain facts side by side, the whole of his testimony.

decisions.choice: one thing I know: testimony from what he has experienced
decisions.reason: Against their "we know" (9:24) the man sets "I know". John's Gospel is built on testimony from what people have seen and heard (1:34; 3:11; 19:35; 21:24), and this man's testimony is of that kind. He cannot judge theology, but he can say what happened to him.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, whoever is speaking, including the leaders who reject him. This applies throughout the passage. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain.

decisions.choice: I used to be blind, and now I can see (B); Before, I could not see. Now I can! (R)
alternatives: I was blind, but now I see
decisions.reason: The familiar form of these words, made well known by older translations and the hymn "Amazing Grace", adds a "but" and a past tense. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the participle in plain words: what he was before, and what he is now.

decisions.choice: yo era ciego, y ahora veo (B); Antes no podía ver. ¡Ahora sí! (R)
decisions.reason: Says plainly what the participle and "now" mean (meaning decision m2). Spanish needs no pronoun for Jesus here.

decisions.choice: moi qui étais aveugle, maintenant je vois (B); Avant, je ne voyais pas. Maintenant, je vois ! (R)
alternatives: j’étais aveugle, et maintenant je vois
decisions.reason: The participle describes what he was, set against "now" (meaning decision m2). "Moi qui étais aveugle" keeps it a description of the speaker, as the Greek does, and avoids the familiar wording of older French versions; Readable makes two short sentences. Literal keeps the participle, "étant aveugle".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun alternatives, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and God is carried at every level by the subject honorific -si-, by "께서" and by "그분".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "he" is in the verb ("ይሁን")
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "ዕውር የነበርኩት" (I who was blind) for the participle "being blind"
decisions.reason: A relative form keeps the Greek participle as one phrase standing for his former state, set against "አሁን" (now); a 'while' clause would say he sees while still blind.

decisions.choice: they question him again on the details of the healing
decisions.reason: He has already told them (9:15). The text does not give their reason for asking again. The setting suggests they are looking for a slip or for some detail they can use against Jesus, such as the making of mud on the Sabbath (9:6, 14); the man takes it so (9:27).

decisions.choice: asked
decisions.reason: The words that follow are a question, so Balanced and Readable say "asked".

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no, asked with irony
decisions.reason: The word that opens the question expects a denial. The man knows they do not want to follow Jesus; the question needles them for their interest in every detail.

decisions.choice: disciples: followers who learn from a teacher

decisions.choice: Surely ... do not (L); Could it be that (B); ... Surely not! (R)

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso ...? (L); ¿Será que ...? (B); ¡Seguro que no! (R)

decisions.choice: vous ne voulez tout de même pas ... ? (L); Se pourrait-il que ... ? (B); ... Sûrement pas ! (R)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no and is asked with irony (meaning decision m1). Each level marks that in its own way, so that the man's needling shows; a plain question would sound like a real offer.

decisions.choice: "... እንዴ?" (L); "ወይስ ... ይሆን?" (B); "... ? አይመስለኝም!" (R)

decisions.choice: reviled: abused him with insulting words
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak abusively of or to someone. They answer his question not with an argument but with scorn.

decisions.choice: you ... that one ... we: emphatic pronouns setting two loyalties apart
decisions.reason: Both "you" and "we" are emphatic, drawing a line between the man and themselves. "That one" keeps Jesus at a distance; they do not speak his name.

decisions.choice: disciples of Moses: faithful to the law God gave through Moses
decisions.reason: The Pharisees saw themselves as students and guardians of Moses' law (7:19, 22-23). They set Moses against Jesus, but John has already said that the law came through Moses and grace and truth through Jesus Christ (1:17), and Jesus has said that Moses wrote about him (5:45-46). To be a true disciple of Moses would be to believe in Jesus.

decisions.choice: that [man] (L); that man (B, R)
decisions.reason: The demonstrative keeps the contempt of their words (meaning decision m2); there is no pronoun for Jesus here, so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: aquel (L); ese hombre (B, R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the contempt of their words (meaning decision m2). "Tú" is the healed man.

decisions.choice: celui-là (L); cet homme-là (B); cet homme (R), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The leaders keep Jesus at a distance with a demonstrative and do not use his name (meaning decision m2). French "celui-là" and "cet homme-là" carry the same contempt; as in the English, they are not pronouns, so no setting applies. Where the leaders do use a pronoun for him (verse 29 "d’où il est"), it takes the setting.

decisions.choice: Discípulo daquele homem é você! (B); Você é que é discípulo (R)

decisions.reason: The Greek stresses both "you" and "we" (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable put the stress on "você" by word order and "é que", the usual Portuguese means of emphasis, so that "mas" is not needed.

decisions.choice: has spoken: God spoke to Moses, and that word still stands

decisions.choice: where he is from: his origin, and so who sent him and by what authority
decisions.reason: To know where a man is from is to know whether his authority is real. Earlier, people in Jerusalem said they knew where Jesus was from (7:27), and Jesus told the Pharisees that they did not know where he came from (8:14). Now the leaders admit it, meaning it as a reason to dismiss him. In John's eyes they have said more than they know: he comes from God (7:29).

decisions.choice: we know: the man speaks of what everyone, the leaders included, believes
alternatives: we, meaning the man and those who follow Jesus
decisions.reason: He takes up the leaders' own words (9:24, 29) and appeals to a belief they share. From it he will argue to the conclusion they will not accept (9:33).

decisions.choice: God does not listen to sinners: the teaching of the Scriptures
decisions.reason: The Scriptures say that God does not hear those who hold on to sin (Psalm 66:18; Proverbs 15:29; Isaiah 1:15) and that he hears the prayer of the righteous (Psalm 34:16; Proverbs 15:29). "Sinners" here means people who go on in sin and do not turn from it. The man's point is that God has answered Jesus, so Jesus cannot be a sinner of that kind (compare 11:41-42).

decisions.choice: God-fearing: devout, reverent toward God
decisions.reason: The word describes a person who honors God in worship and in life. It comes only here in the New Testament. Doing God's will is joined to it, as in 7:17.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" includes men and women, so the pronoun that refers back to it takes the gender setting. Readable says "people" and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: reveres God (B); respect him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the adjective into a verb (meaning decision m3). "Respect" in Readable is meant in the sense of honoring God.

decisions.choice: a ese lo escucha, no gender setting
decisions.reason: After "alguien", Spanish refers back with "ese" and the clitic "lo", which are general here; Readable uses the plural.

decisions.choice: honra a Dios (B); lo respetan (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: turns the adjective into a verb (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "celui-là" (L), "l’" (B) after "quelqu’un"
decisions.reason: English puts "them/him" under the gender setting. French takes up the indefinite "quelqu’un" with "celui-là" or "l’", which read as anyone at all, as in 8:51 and 9:22; the pronouns that take a setting here are those for God ("sa", "il"). Readable says "les gens", as the English says "people".

decisions.choice: craint Dieu (L); honore Dieu (B); le respectent (R)
decisions.reason: The adjective means reverent toward God (meaning decision m3). French has no current adjective with "God" in it ("pieux" drops the reference to God), so Literal uses the verb "craindre Dieu", the biblical phrase; Balanced and Readable turn it into an everyday verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" (inclusive we), against the leaders' "chúng tôi" in 9:24 and 9:29
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the man speaks of what everyone, the leaders included, believes; the inclusive pronoun turns their own "we know" back on them.

decisions.choice: "người ấy", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Người ấy" is already inclusive; the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지 ... 그 사람"
alternatives: a gender span, as in the English "them|him"
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지 ... 그 사람" (anyone ... that person) is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "[말을] 듣다" (L); "말을 들어주다" (B); "기도를 들어주다" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot "hear" a person without an object; Literal brackets "말을". Readable names what God hears, prayer, which is what the man means.

decisions.choice: a esse (L); o (B), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to "alguém", which already means anyone, man or woman; the ordinary generic "esse" / "o" needs no setting (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

decisions.choice: no gender span: "ማንም" (anyone, L), "ሰው" (a person, B) with the generic masculine "እርሱን ይሰማዋል"
decisions.reason: Amharic "ማንም" and "ሰው" already include women and men, and the masculine object suffix is the generic form, so there are not two wordings to choose between. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: from the age: never in all of history
decisions.reason: The phrase means from the earliest times. With "not" it says that such a thing has never been heard of. The Scriptures tell of no one who gave sight to a person born blind.

decisions.choice: opening the eyes of the blind: a work the prophets give to God and to his chosen servant
alternatives: no echo of the prophets intended
decisions.reason: Isaiah speaks of a day when the eyes of the blind will be opened (Isaiah 29:18; 35:5), and of God's servant who will open blind eyes (Isaiah 42:7). The man does not quote these, and his point is that the deed is unheard of; but John's readers may hear in it a sign that the promised age has come.

decisions.choice: born blind: blind from birth
decisions.reason: The perfect participle describes a person who was born that way and remained so, as in 9:1. Healing such blindness is what makes the deed unheard of.

decisions.choice: In all the ages (B); From the beginning of time until now (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom (meaning decision m1) into plain words.

decisions.choice: un ciego de nacimiento, no bracket
decisions.reason: Spanish "un ciego de nacimiento" says it without a supplied word (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Jamás, en toda la historia (B); Desde el principio del mundo hasta ahora (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: plain words for the idiom (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Desde que o mundo é mundo
decisions.reason: The Portuguese idiom for "never in all of history" (meaning decision m1), plain and well known; Literal keeps "desde a antiguidade".

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: he is from God
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the opposite of the if-clause. The man draws the conclusion of his argument: God does not hear sinners (9:31), this deed is unheard of (9:32), so the one who did it must be from God.

decisions.choice: from God: sent by God, as a prophet is
alternatives: coming from God's own presence (the sense Jesus gives it of himself)
decisions.reason: Some of the Pharisees had said Jesus was "not from God" (9:16), and Nicodemus said he was a teacher come from God (3:2). The man means one sent by God, as he has called Jesus a prophet (9:17). John's readers know that Jesus is from God in a deeper sense still (6:46; 7:29).

decisions.choice: could not do anything: a double negative for emphasis
decisions.reason: "Not" and "nothing" together make the denial strong. In the setting the man means that he could have done nothing like this.

decisions.choice: anything like this
decisions.reason: Readable says what "nothing" refers to in the setting (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: algo así
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "nothing" refers to (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: born in sins: they take his blindness from birth as proof that he was born under sin
decisions.reason: They assume what the disciples assumed (9:2), that a man born blind bears the mark of sin, and what Jesus denied (9:3). Without meaning to, they also admit that he was born blind, which they had doubted (9:18).

decisions.choice: entirely: the whole of him, every part
decisions.reason: The word stands with "you": not merely touched by sin, but wholly sinful from birth.

decisions.choice: and you teach us?: a scornful question, with "you" emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out twice. The question means: someone like you has no right to teach men like us. The present tense describes what he is doing, or attempting.

decisions.choice: in sin through and through (B); completely in sin (R)
decisions.reason: "Sin" in the singular is the natural way to speak of a sinful state; Literal keeps the plural.

decisions.choice: trying to
decisions.reason: Readable shows the scorn of the question (meaning decision m3): he is attempting something they think he has no standing to do.

decisions.choice: en pecado (B, R); en pecados (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: the singular for a sinful state; Literal keeps the plural.

decisions.choice: c’est toi qui nous fais la leçon ?
decisions.reason: "Faire la leçon à quelqu’un" is to lecture someone one has no standing to correct, which gives the scorn of the question and the stress on "you" (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "enseigner".

decisions.choice: "ሁለንተናህ" (your whole being, L); "ከራስ እስከ እግርህ" (from head to foot, B)
decisions.reason: Greek "wholly" refers to the whole person; Amharic says it with a noun for the whole self, or at Balanced with the common idiom.

decisions.choice: threw him out: drove him from their presence, and probably from the synagogue community as well
alternatives: only out of the room or court where they questioned him
a formal sentence of expulsion from the synagogue
decisions.reason: The words say that they forced him out. His parents had feared the decision that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue (9:22; compare 12:42; 16:2), and the man has just defended Jesus as one from God. The text does not say whether a formal sentence was passed, but the result was that he was cut off from them. A footnote gives the narrower reading.

decisions.choice: thrown out by the leaders, then found by Jesus
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 6:37, where Jesus says that whoever comes to him he will never throw out. Those who reject the man cast him out; in the next verse Jesus goes looking for him (9:35), as the good shepherd seeks his sheep (10:3-4).

decisions.choice: threw him out
decisions.reason: "Threw him out" keeps both senses open, out of the room and out of the community (meaning decision m1), as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: lo echaron fuera
decisions.reason: Keeps both senses open, out of the room and out of the community (meaning decision m1), and the link with 6:37, where Jesus says he will never "echar fuera" anyone who comes to him (m2).

decisions.choice: jeter dehors
decisions.reason: "Jeter dehors" keeps both senses open, out of the room and out of the community (meaning decision m1), and is the wording French uses in 6:37 ("je ne le jetterai certainement pas dehors"), which meaning decision m2 links to this verse.

decisions.choice: o expulsaram
decisions.reason: "Expulsar" keeps both senses open, out of the room and out of the community (meaning decision m1), as "threw him out" does in English; Literal shows "outside" with "para fora".
